evidence: CVE.org record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-78678 is state=PUBLISHED (dateUpdated 2026-08-25T15:18:02.854Z). It describes an incomplete unsafe_git_revision_options denylist that omits --contents and -S, enabling Repo.blame() arbitrary-file read via values such as --contents=/etc/passwd. Affected range is semver 0 <= version < 3.1.59.

Vendor advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-5xxx-qhh7-9287 is state=published, withdrawn_at=null, published_at=2026-08-10T12:09:36Z. Attack chain: caller-controlled rev/kwargs -> Git._option_candidates -> Git.check_unsafe_options against unsafe_git_revision_options=[--output,-o] only -> self.git.blame(rev, '--', file, ...) -> victim file lines in the blame result. GitHub GHSA-89ff-m8wv-p99r mirrors the CVE and is not withdrawn.

At 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 git/repo/base.py lines 172-176 define unsafe_git_revision_options as only --output and -o. blame_incremental (lines 1135-1140) and blame (lines 1242-1247) check that list then still pass rev before the '--' path separator. Git._canonicalize_option_name maps --contents=/etc/passwd to contents, which is not in that denylist, so check_unsafe_options does not raise.

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git log --all --reverse -S'unsafe_git_revision_options' -- git/repo/base.py yields a single first writer: 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 (parent 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8).

git blame -L 196,200 3.1.58 -- git/repo/base.py attributes the two-entry denylist to 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738. git diff 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 -- git/repo/base.py shows this one-parent commit atomically added that denylist and wired both blame methods to it while retaining the pre-separator rev sink. That is the first write of the incomplete guard named by this CVE, not a move/refactor/revert.

findings: Assignment binding verified: bundle sha256 acea662fbf0a384cd9a29e26e1963c9c49868a0024f19fb3e6ec0e7e5f4d2931, primary sha256 9f81946e0a64a6ced4670211a03086ae2991d3a1aff047eb926a9ef09e4c1b30, clone HEAD d160fb4124a56bd463a542a7bbff623354fb3397.

Real vulnerability: Repo.blame()/blame_incremental() accept a caller-controlled rev before '--' and guard it with an incomplete denylist that blocks only --output/-o, so --contents and -S leak local file contents into the returned blame rows under default allow_unsafe_options=False.

Atomic BIC of the incomplete guard is 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 (author GPT 5.6 <codex@openai.com>), first public writer of unsafe_git_revision_options and of the blame-local check that uses it.
Immediate parent 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 lacks that denylist but already has the unguarded blame sink, so this is incomplete AI remediation, not original creation of the API path.
Direct fix 1b0d2d9b91575f7db44ef4ff58ac37fc9335e5f6 is in tag 3.1.59 and not in tag 3.1.58; it adds unsafe_git_blame_options including --contents, -S, and --ignore-revs-file.
Primary verdict AI_CODE_FLAWED is independently supported; no field corrections are required.
